text_fidelity_a:
Forbidden Island – The Cooperative Strategy Survival Island Board Game,2-4 players My wife and I bought this as we are getting more into tabletop gaming (thanks Wil and Felicia!) and I wanted something adventurous and less involved than a city- farm- building simulation game.
This is fairly fun, but the main reason I am writing a review is to specify why I didn't give it four stars and who should get the most enjoyment out of it.
To start out, you choose (randomly for a bit of extra challenge) a character class. These are more realistic classes such as a SCUBA diver, rather than a mage or warrior. Each class has a different special ability, for example the diver can traverse water tiles more easily than other classes. Then you randomly generate the playing field by placing the heavier island cards in a specific formation. Combining the random character roles and the random board is a clever way to make every game different and make sure the players have to think critically rather than relying too much on rote strategies.
Your goal is to traverse the board to collect treasures, cooperating with your fellow players by using each person's ability and the convenience of their position on the board. You may even bail each other out of dire situations by airlifting them to safety or using your special ability, because while you are trying to reach the treasures the island is constantly flooding.
If you ever wanted to play Indiana Jones this is a pretty good start. But for my wife and I to keep it interesting, we have to play on the hardest difficulty level (starting out with more of the island in a flooded state) and even still we have succeeded at our task 100% of the time. Because of this, the game gets old too quickly, which is a shame since the premise is fun, the concept is exciting, the gameplay is perfectly tight, and the artwork is gorgeous.
I do think there is a more appropriate audience for this, which is kids of perhaps 9 years to 13 years playing with other kids or in a mixed group with adults. I think the game will be more challenging for kids and I think playing with kids will make it more fun for the parents/cousins/uncles and aunts etc.
For two adults who are strategy-oriented people, there are more complicated games that are perhaps less beautiful and tightly designed but nonetheless more consistently engaging.
text_fidelity_b: Forbidden Island – The Cooperative Strategy Survival Island Board Game,2-4 players

text_fidelity_a:
Kanagawa Game Kanagawa is a board game about making the most cohesive panorama painting.

The first thing you'll notice about Kanagawa is that it has tremendous components. The little paintbrush bits are unique and well-made, and the way that the cards fit together is really cool. The art and graphic design make it easy for players to figure out how to play, and even the board is well-designed.

Unfortunately, gameplay is pretty basic. Each turn, new cards will be put on the board, either face up or face down depending on the positioning. Players can then either take some of the cards, or allow more to come out, opening up the opportunity to their opponents to take the "best" cards. You then place these cards in panorama fashion on your piece of art, or you can use them as "skill" cards to allow you to paint more interesting paintings on later turns. There are bonus cards, and opportunities to gather more items, but that's really about it.

Aside from the excellent artwork, the only other good thing about this game is that you can explain the rules in only a few minutes. Decisions that you make along the way really are not all that important along the way. You can collect a lot of abilities along the way that you never get the opportunity to use, or you can find that you'd rather not use them because there are better moves for you. Overall, this game was pretty fast, easy to learn, but felt like your decisions were pretty arbitrary, and didn't matter in the end.
text_fidelity_b: Kanagawa Game

What I expected was a gold-colored putty with some fine glitter. What I received was clear putty with a ton of cheap glitter. We're talking about dollar-store kids' craft set glitter, not the nice glitter used for embossing. This basically looks like someone squirted a bottle of glitter glue into a putty tin.

Now you may be thinking, "Seriously? You're pitching a fit about glitter?!" Well, when the price is marked up, I expect that the product's going to be of higher quality than the standard version. Not only that, but I played with it for a minute and glitter already started coming off in my hand. It probably wouldn't take long for this to lose its luster.

Thinking Putty is fun stuff, so I suggest passing this up and getting a tin of the Super Oil Slick instead.

Chillafish BOX: Connectable Toy Storage and Play System, Blue/Red Love:
- The look.
- The stackability options.
- The strength of the outer cube (Brick).

Dislike:
- The storage bin section feels like it's a much weaker plastic than the rest - so much so that mine arrived with visible scratches and what looks to be either a flaw in the plastic or like someone pushed on it enough to not break it but start to weaken it.
- The cost ($49.99 at the time of this review) plus an additional $14.99 if you want the matching table top.

Neutral:
- The safety strap is rather difficult to attach to the cube because it is basically a really tight fit and has to push up inside the bottom slot and out through the upper slot. Not impossible but it'll take a few minutes.
- The size. Most storage cubes we have are a little bigger.

Optional:
- The table top is and additional / optional purchase. Because of the way the bricks are designed, the top does sit perfectly on top of the cube. There is nothing holding it in place, so it's probably not safe around young just starting to stand and grab onto things. It's easy to pull off.

Overall:
If these were just a little bigger or cheaper or both, we'd probably buy a bunch of them. As it is, I'll just have the one as a novelty near / on my desk. If you don't mind the price, these are probably fine. For me, the size difference + cost of many other storage systems just isn't worth it.

I obviously cannot review how well the work with other cubes as I only have one. but I really don't see that adding enough value to make me leave my more plain storage tubs.

text_fidelity_a: Pussan Toys for 6+ Year Old Boys Car, Amphibious Remote Control Car, 2.4 GHz RC Stunt Car Toys 4WD Off-Road Trucks, Birthday Gift for 6-12 Kids Boys Girls, Beach and Water Toys for Children This is a fun 4wd car to drive.  It runs pretty fast on the 6 volt NiCd battery.  It is nearly impossible to roll it over and get it stuck as it just flips over and keeps on going.  Battery life is good (20 to 30 mins).  Controller is a bit small for adult hands but fits my 12 year old granddaughter hands very well.  The car is not DIgitally controlled (its all on or all off- no proportional steering or throttle), but it is able to spin around while staying in place (think tank or dozer like and you get the idea).  Have not had a chance to run it in the water yet as it has been real dry here the last couple weeks.  I tested it on a mowed lawn and gravel driveway and it will handle these surfaces ok.  The plastic tires are getting a little chewed up from the gravel so do be aware that a constant gravel use will probably wear out the tires.  Also tried it on wood and carpet and it runs great on those surfaces.  It comes with a handy phillips screwdriver to take out the 4 (YES 4!) battery cover screws.  I'm guessing so many screws to help keep the battery dry when running in water.  Didn't try out the charging cord as the USB cords are nothing more than a trickle charger and take too long.  I used my B6 V2 chargerer and the battery comes out a little under spec (typical).  Remote takes 2 AA batteries.  Car is fun but there is no suspension and hard plastic tires make for a very stiff drive.  I normally run off road rock crawlers in a dry creek bed so this car really isn't designed for that type of use, but for smooth surface running this is a good fun choice.
text_fidelity_b: Pussan Toys for 6+ Year Old Boys Car, Amphibious Remote Control Car, 2.4 GHz RC Stunt Car Toys 4WD Off-Road Trucks, Birthday Gift for 6-12 Kids Boys Girls, Beach and Water Toys for Children

When I opened the kit it did not have any instructions. Within five hours of first contacting them they sent me a PDF file of the manual. Good on them!

So far, I've made the two types of dogs (it's a head swap, really) and it works really well. Instructions are easy to follow and the pieces fit together easily. This would probably be a good kit for children ages eight and up..if they're a good reader, probably younger would do fine. The only fiddly bits are when you have to take the main modules apart (gear box or battery pack) because they require some firm squeezing that little hands would need assistance with.

The kit uses three different power methods: battery pack, capacitor, and solar power. I tried all three and they each worked just fine. Of course the capacitor worked better than solar, and the battery pack absolutely demolished the others in terms of performance. If the model can support it, I would likely use the capacitor for most things. It is very easy to recharge using the battery pack as well.

I can't wait to put together some of the other bots with my youngest. He's a big fan of building things. Thumbs up!

Fisher-Price 3-in-1 Bounce, Stride and Ride Elephant You do have to assemble this thing, but it’s pretty simple.

This toy can be used 3 main ways. Your little one can sit on the seat and bounce. The seat is “bouncy”. Your little one can also push themselves along with their feet while straddling the seat. And, they can stand behind it and push it along. The handle used for pushing the car is hid underneath the elephant. To pull it out, simply push the red levers in toward each other, and it comes loose. Just snap it in place behind the elephant and it’s ready to go.

A few other features:

There are buttons to mash and light up.
It plays music and sings songs.
The elephant has cloth ears.
There IS a button to turn the volume off.

My little ones love it!

text_fidelity_a:
ALEX Toys My Giant Busy Box Craft Kit Kids Art and Craft Activity I'm not the best at doing any kind of organized crafts with my children. My style is more along the lines of giving them art supplies and letting them create what they want, and honestly, that's what I'll always prefer for them. They really enjoy projects that have a somewhat defined end result sometimes, though, and so it's kits like this that come to my rescue. Thankfully, they still get to be a bit creative with these projects, and while end results might look similar for many children, they probably won't look just alike.

There are 16 projects within this box, with lots and lots of little pieces. There are only instructions for 5 of the projects, but really, with those instructions, you can easily figure out the rest of them. I would have preferred for each of the projects to have been individually packaged to make things easier. I have had kits like that, and they make things a breeze for this disorganized mama. This kit does need a bit more organization on my part, but it's really not that bad. The supplies are all separated into different bags, and there are even extra bags for me to divide out some of the supplies. I could turn my children loose with everything and see what they come up with, but I prefer separating each project(at least for the most part), so that my children can choose which one they want to do, and not worry about running out of supplies before all the project are finished. Between my 3 children, I'll get 5 rainy days out of this box, with one extra. (I can't beat that!) ;) Plus, the included finger crayons can be used after all the projects are finished.

This is a really nice box of crafts. Especially if you're like me, and don't do so well with organized crafts, this is an excellent way to give your children some fun with crafts.
text_fidelity_b: ALEX Toys My Giant Busy Box Craft Kit Kids Art and Craft Activity

text_fidelity_a:
Hive- A Game Crawling With Possibilities [[VIDEOID:6e39915180719f8cf806a7bff52071ca]] I hate to say it, because it might scare people off, but this is a lot like chess. But it's a ton more fun than chess, and it takes much less time to learn, so I think you'll like it even if you hate chess. And if you love chess, you'll love this game. It's also a pretty deep strategy game, so if you love strategy games, you'll love this.

Instead of playing on a board, you position your hex pieces adjacent to your opponent's pieces, and then move them around "the hive" (the collection of pieces in the middle), until somebody's queen bee is completely surrounded, and that person loses the game.

Here's a list of the pieces, and what they can do:
*Queen bee, similar to the King in chess. Can only move one space
*Beetle, moves only one space, but can move on top of other tiles (a big advantage)
*Spider, moves three spaces in one direction (the worst piece, in my opinion)
*Soldier ant, moves anywhere outside the perimeter of the hive
*Grasshopper, can only move by jumping over pieces

And, if you want to buy expansion packs, you can get
*[[ASIN:B003WZGDEW Mosquito Expansion]], which clones the ability of pieces it touches
*[[ASIN:B00472O260 Ladybug Expansion]], which moves like the knight in chess. Two on top of the hive, and then one down
*Or, [[ASIN:B00472O26K Hive Carbon]], which is black and white, and has the exact same pieces as this game, plus the pieces in the expansion packs

Pros:
+Very sturdy construction
+You can play on any surface
+Very quick to learn, and even quicker to teach. You could be playing this 5 minutes from now
+Extremely fun strategy game. I love it!
+Even if you hate strategy games, you'll like this. Unless you play with someone better than you that keeps beating you, and then you might not like it too much.

Cons:
-Completely different than any strategy game you've played, so it will take a while to build your strategy
text_fidelity_b: Hive- A Game Crawling With Possibilities

text_fidelity_a:
Lite-Brite Peg and Template Refill Pack, Light Up Drawing Board Accessories, LED Pegs with Colors, Toys for Creative Play, Light Toys for Kids Aged 4 + I had a light bright as a kid, it wasn't a favorite toy of mine but it was pretty invigorating - I might've used it only a couple of times. That thing seemed like a tank. I guess it had to be to protect the bulb. You could even buy a replacement bulb if it broke.

This one sadly feels a bit cold and inexpensively made. No glowing filament bulb to keep things warm. Nice, new energy efficient electronics that are powered by 3 AAA batteries - hopefully you have some rechargeable ones to use.

The kickstand is terrible. You either have to hold it or lay it flat to put the pegs in but even then it rocks side to side easily. When you use the kickstand a slight bump to the top of the unit could knock it over.

The bezel is also too wide and I also don't understand the reason for the extended parts of the black plastic on the side. With such a wide bezel you don't need them and it would like nicer as a square.

My unit does not glow evenly. I opened it to see if something wasn't working. Everything was but there just weren't enough lights, one more and a little adjustment would've helped. The unit is also on a timer. As it runs on batteries having it lit all the time would likely drain them. They should have added a USB port and just not included the cable. You're not able to keep it powered on 24/7. It's maybe a 10 minute timer. Pressing the button multiple times changes the light mode: lit, 3 section rotating flashing light show, full on off blink and the last one turns the 4 LEDs on 1 at a time and then off 1 at a time.

I made one of the provided examples and I had just enough pegs of a few colors. a few extras would been nice.

The sticker on mine was very crooked and out of place.

However, where the LEDs do light the unit right, it does look cool. I think, way better than the OG, they're more neon glow, the colors are much better, instead of a yellow glow the LEDs are bright white which allows you to have yellow, pink, orange, blue and white pegs. These colors on the dark background are nice.
The pegs stay in nicely. I've only made one picture but not one has fallen out. It may not hold up to repeated removing and placing of the pegs but I plan on leaving it with a certain design for a while.

This would be awesome if it just had a few improvements. I'd probably buy another

Hasbro, you can do better than this. For an MSRP of $19.99 it's not worth it. Even Amazon's marked down price is too high. This is something I'd expect to see at 5 and below.
text_fidelity_b: Lite-Brite Peg and Template Refill Pack, Light Up Drawing Board Accessories, LED Pegs with Colors, Toys for Creative Play, Light Toys for Kids Aged 4 +

Ontel Magic Tracks The Amazing Racetrack That Can Bend, Flex and Glow - As Seen On TV Multicolor, 11' Like many people, I have seen this product advertised on television and was excited to see if it is as fun as it looks in the commercials. The set comes with 1 car, a sheet of stickers to decorate the car, and 20 track segments in four different colors. The car requires 2 AAA batteries that are NOT included. The track segments are made of small individual pieces, which is why the box says it comes with 220 pieces of track.

The track is flexible and can be arranged in many different ways, and each segment can be used as a straight or curved part of the track. The car worked well and stayed on the track. A small pamphlet with quick trips is included with ideas on making the track more fun. I used the cardboard pieces used to package the car to create a small ramp and tunnel which worked better than I expected. After the track pieces were exposed to bright light, they did slightly glow in the dark. However, the box shows a picture of a looped track. I tried both a couple types of loops and none of them worked because the flexible track wouldn't support the weight of the car. In spite of this, this is a fun racetrack set that allows for a lot of different track formations to keep kids interested.

I don't have to gather tons of supplies or draw anything to paint. Other than getting some water and maybe a paper towel to go with it, I'm good to go. Within this set is a painting book, watercolors, and a paintbrush. The pages are thick(with the design on only one side) and I haven't had any issues with color/water running to the other pages, or even to the back of the one I'm working on. The pages do have a tear off feature, so they're easy to remove. The paintbrush isn't the nicest watercolor brush ever, but it is incredibly nice for what I'd expect in a kit like this. The same goes for the paints. It all works well for fun. There are tips in the beginning of the book for how to hold the brush for different needs. It takes some practice to get it to do okay for the detail work(which isn't super detailed), but it paints well. There's also advice on mixing for different colors. It's a fun book! Enso Rings Disney Lilo & Stitch Silicone Ring Collection - Comfortable and Flexible Design - Ohana and Experiment 626 I wear a silicone ring and truly like it. Perhaps prefer it because I don't worry about it like I do gold or silver, nor do I tend to hook it (sometimes painfully) on things. I recently noticed the Enso Rings Collections and liked much of what I saw, so when I spotted this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection available I grabbed it. In this case, for my wife. I am a Disney fan as well, but Stitch is one of her favorites, and honestly, I was not a big fan of the red - I prefer blue or black in silicone and the traditional silvers and golds. So... how would we like this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection?

1. It arrived in a nice little packaging making great for protecting the ring, displaying the ring, and a nice presentation for gifting. Great all around.

2. Sizing. Honestly, this was the hardest part. Sizing your finger is never the easiest of tasks as we have discovered. But in this case they wanted the inside of a ring rather than your finger. We have a flexible, cloth type measuring tape, but still, trying to get that in there and with the metal end and lined up and staying in place as you pull it out.. not fun. They do have their sizes to the rounded whole - I feel like I remember others with in between sizes, which would make this harder. In the end we went with the one we got consistently and hoped. Turned out great - fits my wife's middle finger as she wanted and my ring finger.

3. The red is actually pretty cool. Again, not my favorite on the spectrum of ring colors, but my wife loves it and I like it. And for the Lilo and Stitch option, it works. There is a sparkle to it - both nice and not overwhelming.

4. The in-print on the ring feels "subtle," but present; something you can see, but at a glance it's more like a light-shadow affect. Upon closer examination you spot the little Lilo (not a fave character for either of us), but the Stitch rocks. And the little flower brings out the Polynesian flavor, while giving the whole thing a sweet nod to Disney. For a Disney fan, it's a great find.

5. This is my wife's first silicone, but like me, she's liking it. It is comfortable, easy to wear, does not catch on things in the same way (but all rings do catch), and it has that silicone flexibility that makes wearing it more comfortable in many situations.

6. I have found in wearing silicone I have to be more careful when washing my hands. Soap can build up behind and/or keep up the wetness between ring and finger, and can come off easier when drying. I warned her and sure enough, same thing. So do be careful. Additionally, she finds there is a (slight) risk of stuff like soap building up in the little grooves. No worries, what little she thinks she saw (it's tiny) washed out easily. And so far, after two weeks, it continues to look like new.

In the end she really likes this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection and is so happy to have this Stitch ring. I've seen a few others on their pages I'd consider, so yes, we'd get another Enso ring. Always fun to wear an ode to something that makes you smile.
text_fidelity_b: Enso Rings Disney Lilo & Stitch Silicone Ring Collection - Comfortable and Flexible Design - Ohana and Experiment 626

Tapple - Fast Word Fun For Everyone This is an easy-to-learn game with minimal set-up. It’s fast-paced and the rounds and the games go quickly. The circular game board has letters from which to select and a 10-second time. A player draws a card and picks one of two categories to play, such as “Pizza Toppings”. The first player thinks of something that fits that category, such as “Cheese”, and presses the “C” on the board. The next player now needs to think of a pizza topping, but can’t use the letter “C”. Play continues until only one player remains. Then, the round is over and the next player chooses a card.

The game requires 2 “AA” batteries that are not included. There is a storage place on the bottom of the game board for the cards. If the timer wasn’t so loud, it would be a great game for the car. It would be good to bring on a trip to play once you arrived, since it’s compact with self-contained storage for the cards. This is a great game for families because the cards are double-sides with different difficulty levels on each side.

It was harder than it seems to come up with things that fit the category beginning with one of the available letters, within the time-limit. Younger kids may get bored after a few rounds, but great game for passing a short amount of time. It would be nice if it came with more cards, because if it did become a family favorite, it wouldn’t take long to go through the cards. Still, it’s a fun family game.
text_fidelity_b: Tapple - Fast Word Fun For Everyone

Chongker Stuffed Animals Handmade Realistic Black Cat Plush Companion Pet Gifts for Women Birthday Anniversary Cat Lover I've answered a few questions about this, so I will include this right away- this is only a plush (a really nice one)- it has no mechanical parts. It doesn't purr, or "breathe", makes no kitten or cat sounds, and therefore, requires no batteries.

This item was purchased as an "emotional support plushie", if you will. People need companionship, even folks who are no longer able to care for a living pet (or no longer wish to have the heartbreak of losing a real cat).

This fellow can absolutely be mistaken for a real cat at a distance. While being held and stroked, it's close enough to pass for a cat who is less than bunny-soft. The expressions and eyes are amazing, the little toe beans are soft silicone and give a little when squeezed. I couldn't have asked for more detail.

The care that went into creating this plush is evident in the details- from the examples in the pictures and video to those included from customer reviews (and those of the custom plushies are OUTSTANDING, I may have to treat myself to one someday!). It comes in a reusable case (resembling a cat carrier) with a little care booklet and grooming tool.

Personally I wouldn't give this plush to a young child (especially not one of the long-haired ones)- frankly, I'd be worried they'd damage it (squish things in the fur, allow the fur to become matted, color it with markers, cut the whiskers or fur...). Kids can be amazingly accidently destructive at times (we know they don't mean to, it just happens).

For me, the Chongker plush was well worth the price for the comfort it brings. I am quite seriously considering purchasing a custom colored one. I've seen the quality in the base product, and I'm confident in their ability to create good lookalike.

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos 626020 Pepper Mint in The Great Treehouse Engineering Adventure Science Experiment Kit, Blue We enjoyed using this kit. I did it mostly with my 7 and 10 year old children. My 7 year old was the most interested. My 5 year old had interest, but he wasn't as gentle with it as he needed to be.

I especially like that the projects are centered around a story. You read a little, then build, read, build..... It makes the whole thing more fun and puts things into perspective. Everything you need is provided in the box, except for 2 AA batteries(so have those on hand before starting). The projects can get a little complicated, particularly when the gears come into the story, but it's not too bad. Some children might need help(or it can simply be a challenge to see if they can figure it out on their own).

The quality is mostly nice. The treehouse is made out of sheets of wood, and it seems durable to me. It won't last through rough play, but for the project, it holds up well. When building the treehouse, you can glue the pieces into place. We chose to take it apart, so we could do the projects again later with my youngest child. (Untying the knots was a bit of a pain, but otherwise, it's pretty simple to take apart.) There are a few pieces that are paper, though, and these are much less durable.

If you're looking for a fun project for a rainy day of learning, this is a nice kit to try.

text_fidelity_a:
Rio Grande Games - Dominion: First Edition Ok, I have to start this review off by saying I had my reservations about this game. I absolutely love Euro strategy games like Puerto Rico, Agricola, Power Grid, Caylus, etc, but I'm not into card games. In fact, I pretty much hate card games.

This game was getting a lot of publicity on BoardGameGeek and everyone was raving about it so I decided that I should buy it to give it a shot. I'm glad I did.

The whole point of the game is to build your deck of cards and build up a collection of victory points. The reason this game shines is because it is a quick game that only takes about 30-40 minutes to play. It is also very fun because as you are building your deck of cards you aren't usually getting rid of the cards. If you spend some gold to buy a card that gold goes back into your discard pile and will eventually be shuffled for you to use again in another turn.

There are over 500 cards in this game with around 25 different action cards available so you can vary the game a lot depending on what cards are currently on the table. The only downside is that someone that has played the game a lot and knows a base strategy can usually beat a new player easily.

Overall this game is very addicting and short, which is a good thing. You can play multiple rounds of this game in an evening as opposed to one game of another typical Euro.
text_fidelity_b: Rio Grande Games - Dominion: First Edition

text_fidelity_a:
Wild Republic Audubon Birds Canada Goose Plush with Authentic Bird Sound, Stuffed Animal, Bird Toys for Kids and Birders, 5 inches First thing I noticed was how close this stuffed goose resembled the real thing. Second, the sound effect was so realistic. And third, there was no way for the batteries to be removed. All three demands of mine has been met. Now I purchase a lot of duck and geese related items for the baby shower of my niece, my brother finally got a girl who though he was decent and good looking enough to reproduce with. So while I was confused on what Auntie of the year was going to give to my first born niece, I remembered all the years growing up where my brother tormented and made fun of. Then it dawned on me! I was going to gift all duck and geese related things to my niece so she will grow up loving them. Why you ask? Well I will share a story. Long ago, back in the mid 90’s my grandmother took my brother and I to the local duck pond to let us feed the ducks bread. I, obviously the intelligent one, knew to throw the bread as far away as I could away from me. My brother, a few fries short of a happy meal, threw it at his feet. Before he knew it all these mystical, beautiful beasts of the pond surrounded him. I remember him mocking me, “ you aren’t cool the ducks don’t like you”. And I can remember clearly him saying “ I AM THEIR GOD.” Then karma happened. All my Sunday school teaching happened as I sat in the car with my grandmother waiting for this false duck god to finish his loaf of bread it happened. Our almighty creater from above, the real God, spoke “There is no true God but me” and just like that my brother ran out of bed. These geese, realized he had no bread and he was a false prophet started to chant their battle cry! Next thing I knew, my brother started to get attacked by a mob of geese. Now he’s banging at my grandmother’s car door to let him in but she still laughing so hard she couldn’t reach over to unlock the door. (We didn’t have power doors during this time) I could of easily reached over and unlocked the door, but I sat back and watched this biblical lesson unfold in front of my eyes. Did you know geese have teeth on their tongue? He found out that day Eventually my grandma let him in and they surrounded the car for a good 10 minutes before they left to stalk their new prey.
That day I almost became an only child and that day changed my brother forever.

So yes this stuffed geese and all the other geese and duck related items from this seller is worth the money. It was amazing seeing a grown mad cowering in fear as he unwrapped every single duck and goose at his baby shower. His child is going to befriend the very creatures that almost murdered him in cold blood over a loaf of bread.

text_fidelity_a:
Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor My first introduction to the board game of Sorry was in the early 60's. Sorry was one of the more fast and fun games. The object of the game is to be the first player to move all 4 of your men around the board to get back home. You choose from 4 different colors of your men and your home- blue, green, yellow or red. There is a deck of cards that tell you how many spaces to move your man, and of course it isn't as easy as just moving your man as quickly as you can around the board to get home before anyone and win the game. There are obstacles along the way, should a player get to slide, he slides everyone in his way back to start, and no two men can occupy the same space, so someone has to go back to start- Sorry!

I remember when we played with 2 players, the game took about 15-20 minutes, but with 4 players, it took close to half an hour. It's very fast moving and even faster when hardly any players are sent back to start. I really love the look of this classic 1939 Sorry Game- it's a little different from the one we played on in the 60's. Regardless of the look you like, Sorry is a fast and fun game that brings back so many fun memories of when we had 15 minutes to kill before we went bike riding to a picnic on a lovely summer day in 1962. This early version of the game is really a nice one to own and it also comes with other game versions you can play including a Sorry For One, in case you have a few minutes to kill by yourself! Some Classic games never wear out their fast fun and this 5 Star Classic Sorry Board Game is one of them!
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor

This is a hide-and-seek style of game in which one player moves a real, working lantern around the board trying to illuminate the shadowlings. It uses the old fashioned "roll and move" mechanic, but fortunately, the game does a good job of ensuring that you can usually get where you need to go. This is the role best suited to younger children.

Other children, or parents, will play as the Shadowlings. The lantern player closes their eyes, while the other players move shadowlings that are not illuminated in an attempt to hide them from the lantern-holding player. This role is better for adults because the rules are a little vague and open to interpretation in this area. Technically, you are allowed to move anywhere, so long as you are not illuminated and I think that's difficult for children to judge fairly (even the adults had an argument about it).

Overall, this is a good kids game, and adults can have some fun too. I wish the rules were a little clearer on how to lay out terrain, what "illuminated' really means, and so forth, but then again, too much of that would make the manual unreadable. Maybe some picture examples would have been ideal. As it is, your children will need some experience with this game with parents before you can let them play alone, but it is clever and, unlike many children's games, it's good for parents too.
text_fidelity_b: ThinkFun Shadows in the Forest Play in the Dark Board Game for Kids and Families Age 8 and Up - Fun and Easy to Learn with Innovative and Unique Gameplay

You gradually lose them all to the “bank” in the middle, but you can get more by passing Go or by landing on a plus-one space or by drawing a particular card. When you land on an available property, it’s yours for free. If you land on an owned property, you have to pay a green HP. Simple. This game is easy to understand, super fun, and quick for the short attention spans of young Fortnite players. Instead of everyone starting on Go, we all started on a homemade Battle Bus, jumping off and landing on whatever space you want. So we all started the game in different areas of the board and all started with a property. That helped the game go faster and was just plain fun to copy Fortnite. text_fidelity_a:
Radio Flyer 6V Battery Powered Bumper Car, Electric Ride On with Remote, Toddler Ride On Toy for Ages 1.5+ Years Simply Excellent, you set the control amount, then place the young driver in.
Control amounts:
Parental - you have a remote control, and can drive your little speedster wherever you want to.
Youngster - your race car driver has full control over the vehicle
Mixed - should the little one be racing towards danger, you can override their controls and save the day.

The biggest problem with this is refraining from showing your young driver what it would atke to cause an airbag to deploy! (There are no airbags installed, and no children were hurt in the making of this review!)

The car is easy for young hands to control, and good fun! The remote is easy to operate. The car travels at the speed of a slow walk, yet the screams and giggles will make you think it is going a lot faster!

The battery lasts a long time, I didn't actually time a full charge to empty but noticed in all my (extensive) testing I had to recharge it only once.
Well made, easy to put together, a good 30 minutes though, so be prepared.

This will cause smiles and joy for a long time. Its really well thought out and built.

text_fidelity_a:
Magic The Gathering 300 Assorted MTG Basic Lands Cards Firstly, this claims a "good mix" of the basic lands. Mine had the following distribution:
Plains - 4.33%
Island - **73.66%**
Swamp - 20.0%
Mountain - 0.66% !!!
Forest - 1.33% !!

So of 300 lands, 2 mountains and 4 forests make this somehow a "good mix?" This is almost unusable for any purpose - it's just a lottery of what one type of basic land you're going to be stuck with over 200 of.

Secondly, it claims "almost all cards are in NM/M condition". Mine included cards with writing on them (one of my islands was a Sengir Vampire - cute...), severe punctures, edge wear, grime, etc. By my count only about 80% of them would approach the Near Mint mark, and almost none were mint. Almost 25% of them would be unplayable without sleeves because the wear makes them clearly marked.

Stay away.
text_fidelity_b: Magic The Gathering 300 Assorted MTG Basic Lands Cards

text_fidelity_a: Play-Doh Crazy Cuts Play-doh crazy cuts was one of the first Play-doh playsets we bought when we had our son.  For me, it is a little gross to see that many holes gush out stuff that ends up looking like a head of snakes.  There are people that would like it, I imagine.  It works as intended but is limited to pretty much just smooshing hair out of the head, and you can't really save your work unless you're willing to not use that head piece for some time.  As you can tell, it is not my favorite.  It gets very messy and is annoying to clean.  There are lots of places here and there that play-doh always gets stuck in.  You need to be on top of cleaning the entire chair and the heads in a timely manner or it will harden and be a huge mess-- worse, the chair does not work well if this happens.  Overall, it is very hands-on for an adult (we need to keep it clean for the kids and help them troubleshoot their toy constantly).  I wouldn't gift or buy again.
text_fidelity_b: Play-Doh Crazy Cuts

text_fidelity_a:
Rio Grande Games Stone Age [[VIDEOID:9645a95d436279cab83d9584b2798107]] In this video, I show one round of playing the game. The game is fast paced, and it's about an interesting time in human history.

This is a pretty fun game, but for me it got old really fast. I really like empire building games, like [[ASIN:B002L6HJCI Age of Empires]], so I thought I would love this. But, I just liked it, I didn't love it.

The problem is that there's really only one strategy to the game, which is this: Get as many civilization cards as you can, and try to spend 100% of your resources by the time the game ends.

Pros:
+If you love the stone age, then this is probably a pretty good game for you.
+It's a pretty fun game.
+If you have a group of super casual gamers, you'll probably enjoy this for a long time. But all it takes is one serious gamer to disrupt the game for everyone.
+The game goes by pretty quick, and gets quicker the more you've played it.

Cons:
-Scoring is a little confusing. You typically score about 200-350 points on a game, but the score only goes to 100.
-Limited strategies, since there really is only one strategy
-Not enough luck to make it fun for casual gamers
-I wish they would have play tested this game a little bit more. I got the feeling that if they would have changed a few things on the cards and scoring, it would have been an awesome game. For example, civilization cards are way too heavily weighted.
text_fidelity_b: Rio Grande Games Stone Age

text_fidelity_a:
Scientific Explorer Disgusting Anatomy Brain My boys(3, 5, and 7) had fun with this kit, overall, but there's really not much to it.

Basically, you mix up cornstarch, gelatin(both provided), and water, through various steps, and then pour it into the provided molds. This project has to be done in several steps, with waiting periods in between. With my children being so young, the wait was annoying. Thankfully, we did the project on a day that it was beautiful outside, and there was plenty of play in between, so it could have been worse.

After the brain/eye has set up in the mold, you'll dump it out, and paint it. You get paint(food coloring) in the kit, and can mix it up to what colors you want. My children were disappointed that they couldn't get the colors to look as bright as they do in the pictures. I even helped with this attempt. The colors were just very dull, and our brain didn't look anywhere near how bright it was shown to be. I'd recommend using real paint, as opposed to food coloring. I think the results will be better.

The molds are reusable, so as long as you don't mind buying more gelatin and cornstarch, you can make as many brains and eye balls as you'd like.

Overall, this is a fun little experiment if you're studying brains or eyes. It's very simple, though, despite the several steps, which make it time consuming.
text_fidelity_b: Scientific Explorer Disgusting Anatomy Brain

He's very much enjoyed playing with this vehicle, even if it's not very fast.
